articles.title: Mixture of Experts: Why Sparse Routing Scales Models Without Scaling Compute
articles.excerpt: A dense transformer pays for every parameter on every token. Double the model, double the compute, no matter how easy the token is. Mixture of Experts (MoE) breaks that bargain. It keeps a huge pool o…
articles.body: A dense transformer pays for every parameter on every token. Double the model, double the compute, no matter how easy the token is. Mixture of Experts (MoE) breaks that bargain. It keeps a huge pool of parameters available, but activates only a small subset for each token. The result is a model that can be far larger in total size while costing roughly the same per token as a much smaller dense model. That decoupling of capacity from compute is the core idea, and it explains both the excitement around MoE and most of its failure modes. This article explains how routing works, why the load balancing loss matters, what happens when routing collapses, and when MoE is the wrong choice. The intuition: specialists, not generalists Think of a hospital.

articles.title: I tried to reproduce four Collective2 Calmar ratios. None of them matched.
articles.excerpt: I spent an evening recomputing the headline statistics on four Collective2 strategy pages. The profit factors mostly hold up. The Calmar ratios do not — none of the four. This is not a fraud hunt. It…
articles.body: I spent an evening recomputing the headline statistics on four Collective2 strategy pages. The profit factors mostly hold up. The Calmar ratios do not — none of the four. This is not a fraud hunt. It is a reproducibility check, the same one I would run on any backtest: take the numbers a page publishes, recompute the derived metrics from them, and see whether they agree. The two definitions I used Calmar ratio = annualized return ÷ maximum drawdown Profit factor = (win % × average win) ÷ ((1 − win %) × average loss) Both are standard. If a page shows all five inputs, its Calmar and profit factor are arithmetic, not opinion. Results Four pages had complete summary blocks on 2026-10-27 (twelve candidates were listed, nine fetched; five showed all-zero stats and were excluded as inactive).

articles.title: The Dual-Layer Document Problem: How to Preserve Official Notary Stamps and Signatures in Word Without Sacrificing Text Editability
articles.excerpt: Legal deeds, affidavits, official certificates, and commercial contracts present one of the most stubborn dilemmas in document engineering: they contain two radically different types of content that m…
articles.body: Legal deeds, affidavits, official certificates, and commercial contracts present one of the most stubborn dilemmas in document engineering: they contain two radically different types of content that must coexist on the same page. Dynamic, Flowable Text: Typed clauses, legal covenants, names, dates, and terms that need to be edited, rephrased, or corrected. Static, Authenticating Graphical Elements: Red circular wax seals, blue notary ink stamps, watermarks, embossed badges, and handwritten pen signatures that certify authenticity. When converting these scanned documents into editable Microsoft Word (.docx) files, conventional tools almost always fail.

articles.title: Your draft changed. Why is it still approved?
articles.excerpt: My local draft-review prototype exported only checked drafts. That sounded like a filtering problem. The more interesting test was whether an edit could keep an old approval alive. An approval applies…
articles.body: My local draft-review prototype exported only checked drafts. That sounded like a filtering problem. The more interesting test was whether an edit could keep an old approval alive. An approval applies to the text someone reviewed—not to a permanent row ID. Test the state change, not just the filter The prototype had three checks per draft: source checked, claim checked, and approved. Editing the text cleared all three. Here is the important browser assertion, using Playwright: const sections = page . locator ( ' section ' ); await page . getByLabel ( ' Draft 1 text ' , { exact : true }) . fill ( ' Edited claim ' ); assert . equal ( await sections . nth ( 0 ). locator ( ' input:checked ' ). count (), 0 ); This verifies the visible checkboxes reset.

articles.title: I built a WordPress migration tool that checks its own work
articles.excerpt: Most WordPress migration tools end the same way: export finished. Finished is not the same as complete. Did every post make it? Every image? Does every old link still land somewhere? Before writing co…
articles.body: Most WordPress migration tools end the same way: export finished . Finished is not the same as complete. Did every post make it? Every image? Does every old link still land somewhere? What breaks when people leave WordPress Before writing code, I collected 300 GitHub issues from four popular WordPress export tools and sorted them by title: 27% were the tool itself crashing, timing out, or failing to install 14% were about images 12% were about URLs and permalinks 10% were about HTML turning into broken Markdown I also read 639 Hacker News comments from 21 threads about leaving WordPress. 111 of them describe a concrete difficulty. The most common were build and deploy work afterwards, losing comments, getting content out, and non-developers losing the ability to edit.

articles.title: I put every government fee on my site in a CSV, with an expiry date
articles.excerpt: Most "how to get a passport in [country]" pages go wrong the same way. They were right the day someone wrote them, nobody wrote down where the facts came from, and nothing tells anyone when to check a…
articles.body: Most "how to get a passport in [country]" pages go wrong the same way. They were right the day someone wrote them, nobody wrote down where the facts came from, and nothing tells anyone when to check again. I run LankaSolve , a static site with step-by-step guides and calculators for Sri Lankan government procedures: passports, national ID cards, police clearance, driving licences, vehicle transfers, EPF/ETF and VAT. It's one person, a few hours a week. So the design question was never "how do I write a lot of pages." It was "how do I keep a few hundred government facts true without a team." Here's what worked. 1. Every fact is a row with a source and a next-check date The core of the project isn't a component. It's docs/sources/source-registry.csv .

articles.title: Hate setting up eSIMs? Gemini might soon do it for you (APK teardown)

articles.body: TL;DR A new SIM Manager connector for Gemini has appeared on a Pixel 9 running the Android 17 QPR3 beta, likely by accident. It lets Gemini set up a new eSIM, convert a physical SIM to an eSIM, transfer profiles, restore them from a backup, and delete them. The connector’s details page also shows the rules Gemini follows, including several things it won’t do, like turning on an eSIM you’ve already installed. Gemini can already work with a long list of apps on your phone, from Gmail to YouTube Music. Now it looks like Google wants its AI assistant to help with something a lot less exciting but much more annoying — setting up your eSIM. You’re reading an Authority Insights story.

articles.title: How 'spacewalking' underwater made me feel like I was really in space
articles.excerpt: Analog Astronaut Commander and Aquanaut Michaela Musilova led underwater simulated “spacewalks” in low visibility to test astronaut safety and communication protocols during simulated space missions.
articles.body: I was breathing just fine through my life support systems, but I kept feeling an urge to double check that everything was ok with my "spacesuit" before heading out on this "spacewalk." I have worn many different types of spacesuits on Earth during my career, but for the first time in my life, I knew that I couldn’t just stop to breathe the air outside if there were an emergency. That's because I was underwater. On this excursion, I was leading a simulated space mission underwater called SEA STAR. My " spacesuit " was actually scuba diving gear, and the simulated spacewalks , or EVAs (Extra-Vehicular Activities), included outings where we explored underwater environments.

articles.excerpt: The four volunteers who lived and worked in a simulated NASA Mars mission for more than a year will exit their habitat on Saturday, Oct. 31, after 378 days of isolation in a facility at the agency’s J…
articles.body: Crew Health and Performance Exploration Analog (CHAPEA) Mission 2 crew members (from left) Ross Elder, Matthew Montgomery, Ellen Ellis, and James Spicer, pose for a photo on Oct. 8, 2025. Credit: NASA The four volunteers who lived and worked in a simulated NASA Mars mission for more than a year will exit their habitat on Saturday, Oct. 31, after 378 days of isolation in a facility at the agency’s Johnson Space Center in Houston. Health and performance data collected from the simulation can help NASA develop methods to counter human spaceflight risks for future Artemis and Moon Base missions. Beginning at 3 p.m. EDT, NASA will provide live coverage of the volunteers’ departure from the Crew Health and Performance Exploration Analog (CHAPEA, pronounced cha-pea’-ah) mission habitat.

articles.title: Astronomers discover the secrets of 'string of pearls' supernova relic and the zombie star at its heart
articles.excerpt: Scientists are still learning about a cosmic 'string of pearls,' a unique celestial relic left by a supernova witnessed by humanity around 850 years ago, which has a zombie star at its heart.
articles.body: Scientists are still learning about a cosmic "string of pearls," a unique celestial relic left by a supernova explosion that humanity witnessed around 850 years ago. That is thanks to the most detailed observation of the dandelion-shaped chains of gas and supernova debris that comprise Pa 30, the only supernova remnant of its type observed in the Milky Way . What makes Pa 30 even more unique is that it has a rare "zombie star" at its heart. Supernovas like the one that created Pa 30 are called Type Ia supernovas; they happen when a dead star called a white dwarf overfeeds on a companion star like a cosmic vampire. This overfeeding triggers a runaway nuclear explosion that usually destroys the white dwarf.
